At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before.

Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen.


ROLE OVERVIEW

Every flight test day at REGENT generates a flood of vehicle data, and the faster that data turns into engineering answers, the faster our Seaglider programs move toward production. As a Mission Software Engineering Intern, you'll own a bounded project of your own in test, ground systems, or vehicle health monitoring — something like telemetry prioritization for constrained radio links, ingest and replay tooling, or a fault-detection prototype — built and verified against recorded data and bench setups. You'll also help build the downstream data path for our test infrastructure effort: the schemas, ingest pipelines, and quick-look analysis tools that turn raw telemetry into something engineers can actually use.

You'll sit within Mission Software Engineering, a team working across navigation and route software, perception and autonomy interfaces, vehicle deployment tooling, and the test and ground systems that support all of it. This team believes rigor should scale with criticality, and you'll see that principle in action as your tooling supports real test campaigns and crew-facing, vehicle-health data. 

If you're a graduate student who wants hands-on ownership of real engineering problems - not a side project, but work the team will actually rely on - we'd love to meet you.



WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own a Scoped Project: You'll take ownership of one focused project in test and ground systems or vehicle health monitoring, such as telemetry prioritization for constrained links, ingest and replay tooling, or a fault-detection prototype.

 - Build the Downstream Data Path: You'll contribute to our test infrastructure effort, helping design telemetry schemas and build ingest, replay, and quick-look analysis tooling that engineers depend on after a test day.

 - Work Against Real Vehicle Data: You'll build and verify your project against recorded data and bench setups, learning how the vehicle's publish/subscribe data model moves information across topics, QoS, and schemas.

 - Test for the Hard Cases: You'll write automated tests that cover the scenarios that actually break systems in the field, including stale, missing, delayed, and malformed data.

 - Get Close to Flight Test: You may support live test campaigns and work with crew-facing and vehicle health data, giving you a front-row seat to how rigor is matched to criticality across the vehicle.

 - Collaborate Across Vehicle Programs: You'll work alongside engineers supporting Paladin, Viceroy, and Squire, picking up context on navigation, perception interfaces, and deployment tooling along the way.

 - Document and Present Your Work: You'll walk the team through your design decisions and findings, leaving behind documentation they can reuse and build on well after your internship ends.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - Graduate-Level Foundation: You're currently enrolled in an M.S. or PhD program in computer science, software engineering, robotics, ECE, aerospace, or a related field.

 - Fluency in Python and C++: You're strong in Python and/or modern C++ (17 or later) and comfortable building and debugging in a Linux environment from day one.

 - Rock-Solid CS Fundamentals: You have a genuine command of software design, data structures, concurrency, and automated testing, and you know how to apply that rigor to real systems.

 - A Distributed Systems Mindset: You're familiar with event-driven or publish/subscribe systems, message passing, and networking, and you think naturally in terms of topics and data flow.

 - Hands-On With Pub/Sub Middleware: Experience with DDS, ROS 2, MQTT, or similar middleware is a strong plus and will shorten your ramp-up on the vehicle's data model.

 - Telemetry and Visualization Chops: Experience with data logging, time-series pipelines, or building dashboards will serve you well, since most project areas center on exactly this kind of tooling.

 - Simulation and Replay Experience: Prior work with simulation, hardware-in-the-loop setups, or log replay tooling for robotic or vehicle software is a bonus, though we'll teach you our specific setup.




WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Collaborative Team Player: You believe that great things happen when teams work together. You communicate effectively and collaborate with engineers, stakeholders, and other cross-functional teams to align on goals and move projects forward. You bring people together, ensuring that everyone is on the same page and moving towards a shared vision.

 - Creative Problem Solver: You thrive on tackling complex challenges and finding innovative solutions. Whether you're resolving installation challenges, debugging elusive electrical issues, or adapting on the fly during integration and test, you bring a practical, inventive mindset to every problem. You don't just patch issues - you improve processes, anticipate downstream impacts, and help turn one-off fixes into scalable solutions that raise the bar for future builds.

 - Adaptable & Agile: In a fast-paced, ever-evolving startup environment, you quickly adapt to changing priorities and requirements. You approach challenges with a calm, resilient mindset, and know how to pivot and adjust your approach as needed, ensuring that progress continues without missing a beat.

 - Innovative Mindset: You’re driven by curiosity and a passion for technology. You’re passionate about driving continuous improvement, embracing new technologies and methodologies to enhance efficiency, quality, and team performance.




WHAT WE OFFER

 - Competitive compensation

 - Housing Stipend available for those temporarily moving to join our team

 - Daily, free catered lunches

 - Learning & professional development opportunities

 - Meaningful projects that make an impact

 - Mentorship & guidance from experienced team members

If you’re ready to take on an exciting challenge, grow with us, and make a lasting impact, we want to hear from you. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, but you see yourself contributing to our mission, we encourage you to apply! We value diverse skillsets and experiences and believe in the potential of passionate individuals to make a big impact.

Equal Opportunity Employer

REGENT is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive work environment. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Forming Our Future together 
 FormFactor, Inc. (NASDAQ: FORM), is a leading provider of essential test and measurement technologies along the full semiconductor product life cycle — from characterization, modeling, reliability, and design de-bug, to qualification and production test. Semiconductor companies rely upon FormFactor’s products and services to accelerate profitability by optimizing device performance and advancing yield knowledge. The company serves customers through its network of facilities in Asia, Europe, and North America. 
 
 Rooted in our core values — Focus on the Customer, Ownership & Accountability, Respectfully & Effectively Communicate, and Motivate & Develop People — we foster an environment where diverse perspectives are not only welcomed but celebrated. Everyone can make an impact here. Whether it's improving products, supporting customers, or positively influencing peers and the community, the contributions of our people matter.

 Shift: 
The regular hours for this position are day shift. 
 
 Job Description: 
 As a Software Engineer Intern at FormFactor, you will gain hands-on experience in a high-tech manufacturing environment and learn about the processes that power today’s electronics. The internship will support software tools and automation used in semiconductor device testing. This role is ideal for an undergraduate student who has completed introductory coursework in C/C++, object-oriented programming, and basic software development practices. This is a great opportunity to apply what you’ve learned in school and gain real-world skills by working closely with experienced engineers.
  
 What You’ll Do: 
 
• Develop and maintain software modules that interface with semiconductor test equipment, measurement instruments and internal test frameworks. 
• Implement C/C++ components that support test automation, data parsing, and device characterization workflows. 
• Apply OOP principles to build modular, reusable components for test automations and analytic tools. 
• Assist in debugging issues across software, scripts, and databases. 
• Contribute to tools that help engineers design probe cards, automate production drawing and data file generation. 
• Participate in code reviews and collaborate with test, validation, and product engineering teams. 
• Follow established development workflows, version control practices, and documentation standards, so the team can work efficiently and accurately. 
• Collaborate with engineers and technicians in areas like equipment, facilities and production to solve problems and improve results. 
 Preferred Qualifications: 
 
• Pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field. 
• Coursework or project experience in C/C++. 
• Understanding of object-oriented programming concepts. 
• Familiarity with basic data structures, algorithms, debugging fundamentals and the ability to reason about performance and memory usage 
• Basic understanding of electronics fundamentals, including voltage, current, digital logic, timing etc. 
• Interest in semiconductor devices, electronics, or hardware-software interaction. 
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, especially when troubleshooting issues that span software and scripts. 
• Ability to work independently on well-scoped tasks and collaborate effectively with engineers across software, test, and validation teams. 
• Clear communication skills for documenting code, reporting issues, and discussing test results. 

 Skills: 
Analytical Thinking, Communication, Cross-Functional Collaboration, Object-Oriented Programming (OOP), Problem Solving, Software Debugging, Working Independently 
 
 Education & Experience: 
Minimum of 1 - 2 years of related experience. Operative/Technician roles will typically operate more complex machinery/processes | Required 
 
 Pay Range: 
$22.10 - $29.03 
 
 Pay Range Explained: 
This role in Livermore, California pays between $22.10 and $29.03 per hour, depending on your experience, skills, and background. Pay may vary in other locations. We offer a full benefits package, including medical, dental, vision, life insurance, disability coverage, a 401(k) with company match, employee stock purchase plan (ESPP), and paid time off. You’ll also be eligible for quarterly profit-sharing bonuses and flexible spending or savings accounts. 
 
 Equal Employment Opportunity Statement 
 FormFactor is an equal opportunity employer. FormFactor complies with all national, state, and local laws that seek to promote equal opportunities for any applicant or employee without regard to age, race, color, gender, gender identity/expression, national origin, sexual orientation, religion, disability, marital status, pregnancy or related condition, military service, or any other legally protected characteristics. These protections apply to all aspects of employment, including but not limited to, recruitment, hiring, training, promotions, and compensation. 

 For roles that are designated as remote-eligible, employees cannot be located in: AL, AK, AR, DE, GA, HI, IL, IA, LA, ME, MD, MS, MO, NE, NV, NJ, NM, ND, OK, PA, RI, SC, SD, TN, WV, WI, WY. This list is continuously evolving and being updated, please check back with us if the state you live in is on the exclusion list. A role is remote-eligible only when it is listed as "Remote" in the job location.

Graduate Software Security Intern - Hypertherm Associates 

 We are looking for a graduate-level intern to join our engineering team and help strengthen the security of our PC-based industrial control software. You'll help prepare our products for the EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) , which requires manufacturers of products with digital elements to build security in from the start, manage vulnerabilities for the full product lifecycle, and keep evidence that they comply.

 You'll use industry-standard and AI-assisted security tools for updates of ongoing, automated assessments of our software, find and rank risks, and contribute to documentation needed for compliance. You'll work directly with software engineers and gain hands-on experience in product security in an industrial setting.

 Key Responsibilities 
 Security assessment and testing 
 
• Run Static Application Security Testing (SAST) and Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST) on application code and interfaces 
• Do Software Composition Analysis (SCA) to find vulnerable or outdated third-party and open-source components 
• Help with fuzz testing, configuration reviews, and checks for common weakness types (for example, the CWE Top 25 and OWASP Top 10) 
• Triage findings, remove false positives, and score severity with the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) Threat modeling and risk analysis 
 
• Build and maintain threat models with established methods such as STRIDE , including data flow diagrams and trust boundaries 
• Help write the cybersecurity risk assessment the CRA requires, and map each threat to a mitigation and its residual risk 
• Assess attack surface, including network services, update mechanisms, licensing and authentication functions, and connections to the industrial equipment Cyber Resilience Act Compliance Support 
 
• Perform a gap analysis against the CRA's essential cybersecurity requirements (Annex I) and help prepare technical documentation for the conformity assessment 
• Help define the Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure (CVD) policy and vulnerability handling process, including the CRA reporting duties for actively exploited vulnerabilities 
• Map controls to related frameworks: IEC 62443-4-1/4-2 (industrial automation security) , NIST Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF, SP 800-218), and OWASP SAMM Secure development lifecycle (SDL) and automation 
 
• Add security scanning to the Continuous Integration/Continuous Delivery (CI/CD) pipeline (DevSecOps) 
• Use AI-assisted tools to speed up code review, vulnerability triage, threat model drafting, and documentation, and check all AI output for accuracy 
• Help assess secure update, code signing, secure default configuration, and secrets management practices 
• Write clear findings reports and remediation guidance for engineering teams 
 Required qualifications 
 
• Currently enrolled in a master's or PhD program in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or related field 
• Solid grasp of secure coding principles and common vulnerability types 
• Familiarity with the Windows operating system and basic networking 
• Strong analytical and written communication skills, and the ability to explain technical risk in plain language 
 Preferred qualifications 
 
• Coursework or experience in application security, penetration testing, or threat modeling 
• Familiarity with the EU Cyber Resilience Act, IEC 62443, NIST SSDF, or similar regulations and standards 
• Experience with industrial control systems (ICS) or operational technology (OT) security 
• Hands-on use of AI tools in security or software engineering work 
• Capture the Flag (CTF) participation, published research, or security certifications (for example, CompTIA Security+, GIAC, or OSCP) 
 What you'll gain 
 
• Real experience delivering regulatory compliance work on a commercial industrial product 
• Mentorship from senior engineers and exposure to the full secure development lifecycle 
• A portfolio of practical deliverables, such as threat models, SBOMs, and assessment reports 
• Possible opportunity to turn the internship into a thesis or capstone project, subject to confidentiality agreements 
 Location : Kent, Washington

 Sponsorship of new applicants for employment authorization, or any other immigration-related support, is not available for this position at this time. 

 Skills:
 
 Hypertherm Associates is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer, and we welcome all applications. We recruit, employ, train, compensate, and promote without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, disability, or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. 
 
 At Hypertherm Associates, we are committed to building an inclusive diverse, flexible, and collaborative environment . If our mission resonates with you, but you don’t meet all posted requirements, we encourage you to still apply.  We will evaluate your application materials and may suggest alternative roles that better leverage your strengths and talents.  For positions with multiple levels, we will evaluate your prior experience to determine the level within our organization you are best aligned based upon the job applying.
